actions.action: Inspect every crevice, leaf joint and under bark for hidden bugs
Cut off and discard infested growth
Regularly clean leaves with lemon-water or dish soap spray and wipe down
Dab individual bugs with a cotton swab dipped in 70% or weaker isopropyl alcohol
Spray or wipe the plant with a microfiber cloth to remove dead bugs
Spray soil top, stems and foliage with neem oil in the evening and repeat weekly for a few weeks
Spray dish soap solution (3-4 tbsp per cup of water) on the plant nightly for a few days
Rinse the plant with water the morning after a spray treatment
Dust the plant with food-grade diatomaceous earth in the bathtub, wearing eye/face protection, as a last resort
Research whether the plant tolerates cold before cold treatment
Place a cold-tolerant plant near an open window or in the fridge/outdoors at about 50°F for 24-36 hours
Order and release beneficial insects such as ladybugs, lacewings or mealybug destroyers

verdict.reason: The answer is about mealybugs, not the confirmed aphids. Neem oil spray, the fix that worked, is only one of eight methods. Nothing in it would likely harm the plant.
